Randomly subsample sequences from FASTA files

Source: R/vtamR_fun.R
subsample_fasta.Rd

Randomly selects n sequences (without replacement) from each FASTA file listed in the fastainfo data frame. This function is useful for standardizing sequencing depth across libraries.

Usage

subsample_fasta(
  fastainfo,
  n,
  fasta_dir,
  outdir,
  use_vsearch = FALSE,
  vsearch_path = NULL,
  randseed = NULL,
  compress_method = "R",
  pigz_path = NULL,
  num_threads = 0,
  compress = FALSE,
  sep = ",",
  quiet = TRUE,
  log_file = NULL
)

Arguments

fastainfo

Data frame or CSV file containing a fasta column with input file names. Files may be gzipped.

n

Positive integer: number of sequences to sample from each file.

fasta_dir

Character string: directory containing the input FASTA files.

outdir

Character string: directory where output FASTA files are written.

use_vsearch

Logical: if TRUE, uses VSEARCH for subsampling (Linux only). Otherwise uses a cross-platform R-based implementation.

vsearch_path

Optional path to the vsearch executable. If NULL (default), resolved via getOption("vtamR.vsearch_path") or the PATH (see get_path).

randseed

Integer or NULL: random seed for reproducibility. If NULL or 0, a pseudo-random seed is used. A non-zero seed ensures reproducible results.

compress_method

Character string: compression method (used only when use_vsearch = TRUE). Options are:

  • "pigz": fastest; requires pigz installed (or pigz_path specified)

  • "gzip": slower; available on Linux-like systems

  • "R": cross-platform; uses R.utils but is slowest Performance order: pigz > gzip > R

pigz_path

Optional path to the pigz executable. If NULL (default), resolved via getOption("vtamR.pigz_path") or the PATH (see get_path).

num_threads

Positive integer: number of CPU threads to use. If 0, all available CPUs are used.

compress

Logical: if TRUE, output FASTA files are gzip-compressed.

sep

Character string: field separator used in input and output CSV files.

quiet

Logical: if TRUE, suppress informational messages; only warnings and errors are shown.

log_file

Character string specifying the path to the CSV log file. The path is resolved with the following priority:

  1. the log_file argument, if explicitly provided by the user;

  2. the vtamR.log_file option set with options(vtamR.log_file = ...), if set;

  3. "vtamR_log.csv" in the current working directory, used as a last resort if neither of the above is set.

To disable logging entirely, set log_file = NA.

Value

Updated input data frame with adjusted file names (if needed) and updated read counts.

Details

It can be applied before or after demultiplexing (demultiplex_and_trim_fasta), but is recommended after merge_fastq_pairs and before demultiplex_and_trim_fasta.

Two implementations are available:

  • VSEARCH-based (use_vsearch = TRUE): fast, but only available on Linux-like systems.

  • R-based (use_vsearch = FALSE): slower, but fully cross-platform.

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
# Fast version (Linux)
fastainfo_df <- subsample_fasta(
  fastainfo_df, merged_dir, "random_seq",
  use_vsearch = TRUE, n = 10000, compress = TRUE
)

# Cross-platform version
fastainfo_df <- subsample_fasta(
  fastainfo_df, merged_dir, "random_seq",
  use_vsearch = FALSE, n = 10000, compress = TRUE
)
} # }
